newsitem.title: CHINA: China to build world's longest liquefied coal pipe.
newsitem.headline: China to build world's longest liquefied coal pipe.

text.p: China is to build the world's longest pipline for transporting liquefied coal at a cost of $450 million, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The 720-km pipeline would run from central coal-producing Shanxi province to the eastern coastal Shandong peninsula, it said.
Construction of the pipeline would allow the use of large amounts of clean coal. It was expected to become operational by 2000, the newspaper said.
The Sino-foreign China Coal Pipelines Co Ltd has been set up with foreign capital to prepare for the project, it said.
The investment, to be raised mainly by foreign partners, was expected to be 3.7 billion yuan ($450 million), it said, quoting company general manager Zhang Tianshan.

The pipeline would carry 7.0 million tonnes of clean coal a year, with much of the product used to fuel two thermal power plants, each with installed capacity of 600 megawatts in Shandong, Zhang said.
Surplus coal will be exported, he said.
